mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 6.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and housing starts below their 12-month moving averages indicates economic contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both INDPRO and HOUST are below their 12-month MAs.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising residential mortgage credit (RSAFS) signals strong household spending, supporting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances during late-cycle expansion when RSAFS is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates improving consumer confidence and construction activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase exceeding 0.5% signals accelerating inflation, prompting expectations of Federal Reserve tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth and rise in unemployment rate signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as recession risks increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate < 0 and UNRATE > 0.3pp from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS growth is negative and UNRATE rises by more than 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing contraction regime (INDPRO < 100), a low industrial production level signals economic slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:current value 103.98 (above 100, so condition not met at decision time)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO is below 100.
